Clipboard is a public notice board on old Android.

Hardcoded API keys leak the moment your APK is decompiled.
HTTP is a postcard. Anyone on the network can read it.
HTTPS without certificate pinning is like a locked door with a master key.
Shared preferences are NOT for passwords. Ever.
MODE_WORLD_READABLE was deprecated for a reason.
allowBackup=true leaks your entire sandbox via adb backup.

WebView plus JavaScript equals XSS playground.
Deep links without validation are open invitations to attackers.

Storing tokens in SharedPreferences is like hiding keys under the doormat.
EncryptedSharedPreferences exists. Use it.
SQL injection still works on Android if you concat strings into queries.

Obfuscation slows attackers, it does not stop them.

Tapjacking uses overlays to trick your users.

Debug builds should NEVER ship to production.

Network security config lets you pin certs without code changes.

BiometricPrompt is safer than custom fingerprint code.

Refresh tokens should live in secure storage, not memory.
Session fixation still affects mobile webviews.

Local broadcasts stay in your app.
